description.p: SuperShot is a native GTK4/Libadwaita screenshot tool for Linux desktops. Captures go through the XDG Desktop Portal on both Wayland and X11, so it works on GNOME, KDE Plasma and any compositor that provides a portal backend. Where no portal is available, SuperShot falls back to the command-line screenshot tools the session already has.
Mark up a capture before sharing it:

ul.li: Arrows, rectangles, ellipses, highlighter, free draw, text labels and numbered step markers
Pixelate and blackout redaction that destroys the underlying pixels instead of covering them
Crop with a live selection, and undo/redo across the whole session
Copy the annotated image straight to the clipboard, without saving a file

description.p: And everything the capture itself needs:

ul.li: Capture modes: ask, area, window, or the whole screen
Configurable delay of none, 3, 5 or 10 seconds with a visual countdown
Image editor: rotate, flip, brightness, contrast, blur, sharpen, grayscale, invert
Customisable watermark with 5 date formats, custom text, 4 corner positions and colour choice
PNG and JPEG output with adjustable quality
Clickable desktop notifications
CLI headless mode for scripting and keyboard shortcuts
14 language translations

screenshot.caption: Main application window with capture settings

ul.li: Annotation toolbar: arrow, rectangle, ellipse, highlighter, free draw, text labels and numbered step markers, with an eight-colour palette and adjustable thickness
Pixelate and blackout redaction that destroys the underlying pixels rather than covering them
Undo and redo across annotations, crops and adjustments
Copy the annotated image directly to the clipboard without saving a file
Explicit capture modes: ask, area, window, whole screen — in the interface and on the command line
Configurable JPEG quality
About dialog with the running version, and a --doctor flag reporting display server, portal availability and detected fallback tools
--edit opens the annotation editor on an image already on disk, without capturing
arm64 packages and an AppImage build
Cropping and then saving wrote the full uncropped image and discarded every adjustment made before the crop
The preview window left a wide empty band beside the image, and forced itself to be 1629 pixels wide; tools now live in a collapsing sidebar and the window minimum is 365 pixels

The 14 translations were never installed by any package and the catalog directory was hard-coded to /usr/share/locale, so no localisation ever loaded outside a distribution install; the interface itself was also largely untranslated
Watermark and annotation text is laid out with Pango, so CJK, Devanagari and right-to-left scripts render instead of appearing as empty boxes
Wayland sessions without a Screenshot portal now fall back to grim/slurp, spectacle, wayshot and hyprshot
The display backend is read from GDK rather than the environment, so GDK_BACKEND=x11 inside a Wayland session correctly enables the X11 fallbacks
Portal requests are parented to the window, so the portal dialog no longer opens behind or unfocused on KDE and wlroots compositors
Save paths and folder-opening URIs are built through GIO, fixing directories containing spaces or non-ASCII characters
A missing xdg-user-dirs configuration no longer discards the capture
Temporary captures use a private 0700 directory instead of a predictable path in /tmp
Rendering and encoding run off the main thread, so large captures no longer freeze the interface
Headless captures now copy to the clipboard and post a notification, and no longer create a stray main window
The watermark timestamp shown in the preview is the one written to the file

description.p: Security and dependency maintenance. Snap rebuild to incorporate Ubuntu Security Notice USN-8495-1 (libnghttp2-14). Updated Rust crates to their latest compatible versions (GTK4/Libadwaita stack, zbus/zvariant, tokio, regex, chrono and others).
Security maintenance. Snap rebuild to incorporate Ubuntu Security Notice USN-8269-1 (libavahi-client3, libavahi-common-data, libavahi-common3).

Security and stability maintenance. Snap rebuild incorporates Ubuntu Security Notices USN-8227-1 (libcurl3t64-gnutls) and USN-8233-1 (libnghttp2-14). Hardened pixbuf-to-image conversion and crop bounds checks; clamped watermark text length; canonicalized save directories; rotation arithmetic uses rem_euclid; zoom percentage rounded. Transitive dependency bumps (tokio, zvariant, profiling).
Updated Rust crates to latest compatible versions. Added liblcms2-2 to snap stage packages for security maintenance. Migrated from load_from_data to load_from_string for GTK 4.12+ compatibility.
Image editor with rotate, flip, brightness, contrast, blur, sharpen, grayscale, and invert. Apply/undo crop. Portal-first capture on both Wayland and X11.

Tabbed interface (Shot/Settings). Customizable watermark with 5 date formats, custom text prefix, 4 corner positions, and white/black color selection. Preview window with live watermark overlay and drag-to-crop. PNG/JPEG format selection, custom save directory, Ctrl+Enter keyboard shortcut. Clickable notifications, duplicate file prevention, and branded filenames.
First public release with English UI, i18n support (14 languages), GSettings persistence, desktop notifications, visual countdown, and CLI headless mode.
